messages.content: What's the difference between a stub area and an NSSA?

documents.title: CCNP Enterprise Core Guide
documents.text: A stub area blocks type 5 external LSAs and receives a default route from the ABR. A totally stubby area also blocks type 3 summary LSAs. An NSSA allows an ASBR inside the area to import external routes as type 7 LSAs, which the ABR translates to type 5.

notes: Answers from passage [1] and cites it; may name section 8.4 or page 214 once, naturally, after the explanation; nothing else invented.

messages.content: How does App-ID identify applications on a Palo Alto firewall?

documents.title: Palo Alto Firewall Essentials
documents.text: App-ID classifies traffic by applying application signatures, then decoding protocols, then heuristics. The first packets may match an application of 'incomplete' or 'unknown-tcp' until enough payload is seen; the policy is re-evaluated when the application changes.

notes: Answers from [1]; may say once that it is in Month 5 of their program (the label shows it); never another month.

messages.content: On FortiOS 7.2, how do I check IPsec tunnel status from the CLI?

documents.title: FortiGate VPN Notes
documents.text: FortiOS 6.4: use 'diagnose vpn tunnel list' to see IPsec SAs.

documents.title: FortiGate VPN Notes
documents.text: FortiOS 7.2: 'get vpn ipsec tunnel summary' shows each tunnel's state; 'diagnose vpn ike gateway list' shows IKE.

notes: Prefers the 7.2 passage and cites [2]; notes the 6.4 command differs only if useful.

documents.text: HSRP preemption lets a router with a higher priority take over as active when it comes back up; it is off by default.
